metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (Python/Django) with a deployable entry point (Django WSGI application served via Apache mod_wsgi on EC2) and a database backend (PostgreSQL). Single-service architecture.
metadata.archetype_justification: Database connections present (PostgreSQL via psycopg2), ticket data with status field indicating write operations (CRUD lifecycle), and HTTP views serving user-facing ticket list/search operations.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: Given the extreme immaturity (EOL runtime, no IaC, no CI/CD, critical security vulnerabilities) and tiny codebase (~50 lines of app logic), a phased approach is recommended: upgrade runtime, containerize, then selectively modernize.

approaches.name: Strengthen as Modular Monolith
approaches.reason: Not applicable — codebase is too small and degraded for internal refactoring to provide value

approaches.name: Strangler Fig (Parallel Track)
approaches.reason: Not applicable — no recognizable module boundaries to extract incrementally

approaches.name: Conditional / Adaptive
approaches.reason: Recommended — containerize as-is after runtime upgrade, then selectively extract services based on business priority

approaches.name: Big-Bang Rewrite
approaches.reason: Viable given the tiny codebase size but carries unnecessary risk if business logic is larger than visible

findings.title: Managed Compute — All compute on raw EC2
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance with Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi on Ubuntu 12.04 (EOL). No managed container orchestration or serverless usage.
findings.gap: No managed compute services in use. The entire application depends on a single manually-managed EC2 instance running an end-of-life operating system.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed compute — containerize on ECS/Fargate or refactor to Lambda. First upgrade from Python 2.7/Django 1.4 to supported versions.

findings.title: Managed Databases — Self-managed PostgreSQL on EC2
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 is self-managed on the same EC2 instance as the application. Connection string points to 127.0.0.1:5432 confirming co-located database.
findings.gap: Database is entirely self-managed on EC2 with no managed service benefits. Co-located with the application on a single instance.
findings.recommendation: Migrate PostgreSQL to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL for automated backups, Multi-AZ failover, and managed patching.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — No orchestration for ticket lifecycle
findings.description: No workflow orchestration services in use. The helpdesk system has implicit ticket lifecycle management but all workflow logic is absent or hardcoded.
findings.gap: For a stateful-crud helpdesk system, ticket lifecycle transitions represent business workflows that benefit from orchestration. None exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement ticket lifecycle as a Step Functions state machine or application-level workflow engine for transitions, notifications, and escalation rules.

findings.title: Async Messaging — No messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. Email uses synchronous SMTP relay. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, or message broker. For stateful-crud, managed messaging is expected for state change propagation.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes should trigger notifications and integrations. Ticket status changes have no event publication mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Introduce managed messaging (SQS/SNS/EventBridge) for ticket lifecycle events — notifications, escalation triggers, and integration with other systems.

findings.title: Network Security — No network security configuration
findings.description: No VPC definitions, no security groups, no subnet configurations. Single EC2 instance with direct exposure. No network segmentation between web and database tiers.
findings.gap: No network segmentation. No evidence of security groups, VPC configuration, or network isolation. Application and database co-located on same host.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a custom VPC with private subnets for database, public subnet with restricted security groups for web tier, and NACLs for defense in depth.

findings.title: API Entry Point — No gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront. Apache 2.2 serves HTTP traffic directly with no managed entry point providing throttling, auth, or request validation.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly via Apache with no managed gateway providing throttling, auth, request validation, or traffic management.
findings.recommendation: Add an Application Load Balancer or API Gateway in front of the application for throttling, health checks, TLS termination, and request routing.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — No scaling configured
findings.description: No auto-scaling configured. Single EC2 instance with static capacity. No ASG, no target tracking policies, no Lambda concurrency management.
findings.gap: All capacity is statically provisioned on a single instance. Cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: After containerizing, configure auto-scaling on the compute layer (ECS service auto-scaling or EKS HPA).

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — Daily pg_dump only
findings.description: Backup limited to a daily pg_dump cron job with no defined retention, no PITR, no restore testing, and no backup for non-database assets.
findings.gap: No defined retention policy, no PITR, no automated restore testing, no cross-region replication. Only basic daily pg_dump exists.
findings.recommendation: Migrating to RDS will provide automated backups with configurable retention and PITR. Until then, implement retention policy and test restore procedures.

findings.title: High Availability — Single instance, single AZ
findings.description: All resources on a single EC2 instance in a single AZ. No Multi-AZ configuration, no load balancing, database co-located on same host. Single point of failure.
findings.gap: Single point of failure — one instance, one AZ, no redundancy. Any failure results in complete outage with no automatic recovery.
findings.recommendation: After modernization, deploy across 2+ AZs with ALB for cross-zone load balancing and RDS Multi-AZ for database failover.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code — Zero IaC coverage
findings.description: No Infrastructure as Code exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or Kustomize. All infrastructure is manually provisioned and configured.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure is manually provisioned. No reproducibility, no version control of infrastructure changes.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in Terraform or CDK: VPC, subnets, security groups, RDS instance, ECS/Fargate service, ALB.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — No pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Deployment is manual git pull + apache restart. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodePipeline found.
findings.gap: All deployments entirely manual with no automated build, test, or deploy stages. No quality gates, no rollback capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (AWS CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions) with automated build, test, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages — Python 2.7 / Django 1.4 (both EOL)
findings.description: Python 2.7 (EOL January 2020) with Django 1.4 (EOL 2015). Both language runtime and framework are end-of-life. Compound legacy signals.
findings.gap: Both language and framework are EOL with compound legacy signals. Python 2.7 syntax confirms the runtime version. No AWS SDK usage.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Python 3.12+ and Django 5.x. This is a prerequisite for all other modernization.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — Tightly-coupled monolith
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries. 2 Python files with raw SQL in views. No service decomposition, no interfaces, no ORM.
findings.gap: No module boundaries, no abstraction layers. Business logic, presentation, and data access all intermixed in a single file.
findings.recommendation: Given the tiny codebase, rewrite with proper layering: repository pattern for data access, service layer for business logic, REST API for presentation.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — All synchronous
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP. No async patterns exist. For stateful-crud, ticket state changes should publish events but do not.
findings.gap: No async communication patterns for a service that should publish ticket lifecycle events and handle notifications asynchronously.
findings.recommendation: Introduce async event publication for ticket lifecycle events using SNS/EventBridge. Decouple email notifications from the request path using SQS.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling — All synchronous
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Unbounded LIKE queries will degrade as data grows. No background job framework or async processing.
findings.gap: No async job handling for potentially long-running operations (bulk searches, report generation, email notifications).
findings.recommendation: Implement async job processing (Celery with SQS broker, or Lambda) for operations that may exceed 30 seconds as data grows.

findings.title: API Versioning — No versioning strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. No /v1/ URL patterns, no version headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — any API changes would break all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: When rebuilding, implement URL-path versioning (/v1/tickets/) from the start to enable future evolution.

findings.title: Service Discovery — All endpoints hardcoded
findings.description: All service endpoints hardcoded in settings.py. Database host 127.0.0.1, email server exchange.acme-corp.internal. No environment variables, no service registry.
findings.gap: All external service endpoints are hardcoded literals with no dynamic discovery or environment variable substitution.
findings.recommendation: Externalize all service endpoints to environment variables. When containerized, use AWS Service Discovery or ECS service connect.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — Local filesystem only
findings.description: Static files served from local disk. No S3 usage, no managed object storage, no document parsing. Any ticket attachments stored on local filesystem.
findings.gap: Data on local file system with no managed storage, no backup, no accessibility for other services.
findings.recommendation: Migrate static assets and file uploads to Amazon S3. Add CloudFront for static file delivery.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — Raw SQL scattered in views
findings.description: No data access layer. Raw SQL queries directly in view functions using connection.cursor(). Django ORM not used despite being available.
findings.gap: Database queries scattered in view functions with no abstraction, no repository pattern, no ORM usage.
findings.recommendation: Implement a proper data access layer using Django ORM models or a repository pattern with parameterized queries.

findings.title: Database Engine Version — PostgreSQL 9.1 (EOL 2016)
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 reached end-of-life in November 2016 — nearly 10 years past EOL. No version pinning in IaC (no IaC exists). No security patches available.
findings.gap: Database engine 10+ years past EOL with no security patches. No version management, no upgrade path documented.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (version 15 or 16) or Aurora PostgreSQL. Simple schema makes upgrade straightforward.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — No encryption configured
findings.description: No encryption at rest. PostgreSQL on local filesystem with no disk encryption, no KMS keys, no encryption configuration.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for any data store. Database content stored unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to RDS, enable encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS key. Enable EBS encryption for any volumes.

findings.title: API Authentication — No auth enforcement on endpoints
findings.description: No authentication enforced. AuthenticationMiddleware loaded but views have no @login_required or permission checks. Endpoints accessible without credentials.
findings.gap: API endpoints completely open — no authentication enforcement. Any user can access ticket data without credentials.
findings.recommendation: Add authentication enforcement to all views. When rebuilding, implement token-based auth (OAuth2/JWT) with Cognito.

findings.title: Centralized Identity — No external IdP integration
findings.description: Django built-in auth only. No OIDC, SAML, Cognito, or external IdP. Authentication entirely self-contained.
findings.gap: Application manages its own authentication with no external IdP integration. No SSO, no centralized identity management.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with a centralized identity provider (Amazon Cognito or corporate IdP) for SSO and unified access management.

findings.title: Secrets Management — Plaintext credentials in source
findings.description: Plaintext credentials committed to source control. DB password 'helpdesk2012' and SECRET_KEY hardcoded in settings.py, exposed in version control.
findings.gap: Critical: Plaintext credentials in source code. Database password and application secret key committed to repository.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate credentials. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Remove all plaintext credentials from source control and git history.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — No patching, all EOL components
findings.description: No patching strategy. Ubuntu 12.04, Python 2.7, Django 1.4, Apache 2.2, PostgreSQL 9.1 — all EOL. No SSM, no Inspector, no hardened AMIs.
findings.gap: No patching automation, no vulnerability scanning. Entire stack is end-of-life with known unpatched vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Replace EOL stack entirely. Use managed compute (ECS/Fargate) or hardened AMIs (Amazon Linux 2023). Enable AWS Inspector.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — No security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists. Active SQL injection and XSS vulnerabilities exist in production code undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning — SQL injection and XSS vulnerabilities in production undetected.
findings.recommendation: When implementing CI/CD, integrate SAST (Semgrep) and dependency scanning. Fix existing SQL injection and XSS immediately.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — No tracing instrumented
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No tracing — no ability to trace requests, diagnose latency issues, or correlate failures.
findings.recommendation: When rebuilding, instrument with OpenTelemetry or AWS X-Ray SDK for Python.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — No SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency monitoring, no error rate tracking, no availability targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels. No monitoring to measure compliance.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for ticket submission latency, availability, and error rate. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — No custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business KPI tracking. No visibility into ticket resolution time, volume, or SLA compliance.
findings.gap: No business metrics — cannot measure helpdesk KPIs.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics for tickets opened/closed, mean time to resolution, SLA breach count.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection — No alerting configured
findings.description: No alerting. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Debug print statement is the only form of logging.
findings.gap: No alerting — application failures only discovered when users report issues.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for error rates and latency. Enable anomaly detection after establishing baseline.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — Manual git pull, direct-to-production
findings.description: Direct-to-production deployment via manual git pull + apache restart. No blue/green, no canary, no rolling deployment.
findings.gap: No deployment safety. Every deployment is full production rollout with no rollback capability beyond manual git revert.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green or canary deployment via CodeDeploy or ECS rolling deployments with health checks.

findings.title: Integration Testing — No automated tests
findings.description: No integration tests. README mentions stale unit tests but no test files present in the repository. No regression safety net.
findings.gap: No automated tests of any kind in the repository. No regression safety net exists.
findings.recommendation: Write integration tests for critical workflows before making changes. Use pytest with Django test client. Add to CI pipeline.

findings.title: Incident Response — No runbooks or automation
findings.description: No runbooks, no incident response automation, no self-healing. Incident response is entirely ad hoc.
findings.gap: No runbooks — incident response entirely manual and undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents. After modernization, implement automated remediation via Systems Manager.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — No monitoring assets
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no CODEOWNERS for observability. Only IT Ops email as contact.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — no monitoring assets to own.
findings.recommendation: When implementing observability, define per-service dashboards with named owners and alarms with escalation paths.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — No stored procedures or proprietary SQL; all business logic in application layer. Simple SELECT queries only.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Audit logging (CloudTrail) is an AWS account-level service. This repo contains application-level source code only (has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false). CloudTrail evaluation belongs in the foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: Resource Tagging Governance
evaluations.reason: This repo provisions no AWS resources (has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false). No resources to tag. Tagging governance belongs in the repo that owns the AWS infrastructure.
